label: <DEL> or first-seen trigger token (c/a/2/0/k) after a prefix rich in g/m/3/e/x/t
explanation: Fires almost only in the input phase: about 55% of activation mass is on the <DEL> step (7% of delimiter steps fire), and the rest is on original-phase inputs, mostly the first occurrence of c (strongest), a, 2, 0, k, plus d and n more weakly. It never fires at t<2 and is essentially silent in the copy phase (27 of 12.8k activations). Firing rate goes up with position and with L (L=9 has the highest rate; to_go 7-8 is elevated). Whether it fires depends on which tokens came earlier: a prefix with several of 3/g/m/e/x/t (first_tok and next_out lift 3-5x for 3, g, m) makes firing much more likely. Repeated inputs (in_first=0) rarely fire. The trigger-token x prefix-content predicate keeps about 77% of activation mass but has low precision (about 18% on dev). Most <DEL> or c steps with a suitable-looking prefix stay below threshold, so the gating looks like a graded, distributed function of prefix content that a boolean predicate cannot capture. A weighted count of prefix tokens did not help much (best dev F1 about 0.34). Magnitude claims beyond this are unchecked.
